public_rationale: This forecast has no deadline. It says LLMs, through always-on gadgets, will know everything you say and be able to talk you into almost anything. As of October 2026, OpenAI had not released any consumer device. July 2026 reports said its planned device would learn about its owner and draw on things like email. That points the way Marcus warned but is still unreleased. No decisive event shows such devices capturing everything users say or persuading them broadly, and nothing rules it out either.
limitations: The wording is hyperbolic, so any test requires interpretation.
Evidence on the device comes from anonymous-source reporting.

from_speaker: LLMs will know everything you say
be in perfect position to use that knowledge
to talk you into almost anything
(context) via always-worn gadgets like the necklace
our_interpretation: Read as a forecast with no deadline: LLM-powered always-on gadgets will capture essentially all of a user's speech, and LLMs will use that knowledge to persuade users across nearly any decision.
'Perfect position' and 'almost anything' are rhetorical. A fair test needs widely deployed devices capturing all of a user's speech, plus evidence of broad, effective persuasion using that data.
criteria.support_condition: Widely used LLM devices or services capture essentially all of a user's speech, and studies or documented cases show LLMs using that knowledge to persuade users across a wide range of decisions.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Hard to establish for an open-ended forecast. Strong evidence that deployed LLMs with full personal context have only narrow or weak persuasive effects would count against it.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Wide deployment of always-listening LLM devices, together with independent research or documented cases showing those systems using captured personal speech to persuade users across many kinds of decisions, or strong evidence that they cannot.
